## Questions

### 1. Mystery constant

Suppose $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function (pmf) $p_X(x) = c(4- x)$ for $x$ in $\{-1, 2, 3\}$ and $p_X(x) = 0$ otherwise.

#### Part a

What is the value of $c$ that makes $p_X(x)$ a valid pmf?

::: answer
$c = \dfrac{1}{8}$
:::

#### Part b

Write the piecewise pmf of $X$ and make a plot of it. (You can draw the plot by hand or make it in R.)

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

What is the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of $X$? Write the piecewise CDF.

::: answer
$$F_X(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & x < -1 \\ \frac{5}{8} & -1 \leq x < 2 \\ \frac{7}{8} & 2 \leq x < 3 \\ 1 & x \geq 3 \end{cases}$$
:::

#### Part d

Make a plot of the CDF. (You can draw the plot by hand or make it in R.)

::: answer
Not given
:::

### 2. Wastebasket basketball

Chris tries to throw a ball of paper in the wastebasket behind his back (without looking). He estimates that his chance of success each time, regardless of the outcome of the other attempts, is $1/3$. Let $X$ be the number of attempts required. If he is not successful within the first 5 attempts, then he quits, and he lets $X = 6$ in such a case.

#### Part a

Write the piecewise pmf of $X$ and make a plot of it. (You can draw the plot by hand or make it in R.)

::: answer
$$p_X(x) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{x-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) & x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 \\ \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{5} & x = 6 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$
:::

#### Part b

Write the piecewise CDF of $X$ and make a plot of it. (You can draw the plot by hand or make it in R.)

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Simulate 10,000 trials of this experiment in R. Use your simulation to plot the approximate pmf of $X$ and to check your answers to Parts a and b.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q2-simulate"

set.seed(3333)
reps <- 10000

throws <- expand_grid(sim = 1:reps, attempt = 1:5) |>
  mutate(result = sample(c("in", "miss"), size = n(), replace = TRUE,
                         prob = c(1/3, 2/3)),
         X_if_first = if_else(result == "in", attempt, 6))

X_sims <- throws |>
  group_by(sim) |>
  summarise(X = min(X_if_first))

X_approx <- X_sims |>
  group_by(X) |>
  summarise(prop = n() / reps) |>
  mutate(approx_cdf = cumsum(prop))
```

```{r}
#| label: "q2-plot"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(X_sims, aes(x = X, y = after_stat(prop))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:6) +
  labs(title = "Approximate pmf of X",
       x = "Number of attempts (x)",
       y = "Relative frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: "q2-table"

knitr::kable(X_approx, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("x", "Approximate pmf", "Approximate CDF"))
```

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to the exact pmf and CDF from Parts a and b.
:::

### 3. Sore arm after a flu shot

Suppose 20% of adults have a sore arm the day after getting a flu shot. A pharmacy gives flu shots to $n = 10$ adults one morning. Assume that whether one adult gets a sore arm is independent of the other adults. Let $X$ be the number of these 10 adults who have a sore arm the next day.

#### Part a

Explain why $X$ is a binomial random variable. What are the parameters $n$ and $p$?

::: answer
$X \sim \text{Binom}(n = 10, p = 0.2)$
:::

#### Part b

Write the pmf of $X$. Then use it to calculate $\mathbb{P}(X = 3)$ by hand.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Use `dbinom()` in R to calculate $\mathbb{P}(X = x)$ for every possible value of $X$, and make a bar plot of the pmf. (You can draw the plot by hand or make it in R.) Does your answer from Part b match?

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q3c-pmf"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

n <- 10
p <- 0.2

sore <- tibble(x = 0:n, prob = dbinom(x, size = n, prob = p))

ggplot(sore, aes(x = x, y = prob)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:n) +
  labs(title = "pmf of X",
       x = "Number of adults with a sore arm (x)",
       y = "Probability") +
  theme_minimal()
```

`dbinom()` should match your answer in Part b.
:::

#### Part d

Find $\mathbb{P}(X \leq 2)$ two ways: by hand using the pmf, and with `pbinom()` in R.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part e

Simulate 10,000 mornings at the pharmacy (each with 10 adults) to check your answers to Parts b and d.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q3e-simulate"

set.seed(1010)
reps <- 10000

sore_sims <- expand_grid(sim = 1:reps, person = 1:n) |>
  mutate(outcome = sample(c("sore", "not sore"), size = n(), replace = TRUE,
                          prob = c(p, 1 - p))) |>
  group_by(sim) |>
  summarise(X = sum(outcome == "sore"))

shortcut_sims <- tibble(X = rbinom(n = reps, size = n, prob = p))
```

-   With `sample()`: $\mathbb{P}(X = 3) \approx$ `r round(mean(sore_sims$X == 3), 3)` and $\mathbb{P}(X \leq 2) \approx$ `r round(mean(sore_sims$X <= 2), 3)`
-   With `rbinom()`: $\mathbb{P}(X = 3) \approx$ `r round(mean(shortcut_sims$X == 3), 3)` and $\mathbb{P}(X \leq 2) \approx$ `r round(mean(shortcut_sims$X <= 2), 3)`

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to your answers in Parts b and d.
:::

### 4. Lab processing time

A lab processes blood samples. Suppose the processing time $X$ (in minutes) for a sample is equally likely to be anywhere between 20 and 50 minutes. So $X$ has pdf $f_X(x) = c$ for $20 \leq x \leq 50$, and $f_X(x) = 0$ otherwise.

#### Part a

What is the value of $c$ that makes $f_X(x)$ a valid pdf?

::: answer
$c = \dfrac{1}{30}$
:::

#### Part b

Find $\mathbb{P}(30 \leq X \leq 40)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Find $\mathbb{P}(X > 45)$.

::: answer
$\mathbb{P}(X > 45) = \dfrac{1}{6} \approx 0.167$
:::

#### Part d

Find $\mathbb{P}(X = 35)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part e

Simulate 10,000 processing times in R with `runif()` and use them to check your answers to Parts b–d.

::: answer
```{r}
#| label: "q4e-simulate"

set.seed(4141)
reps <- 10000

lab_sims <- tibble(x = runif(n = reps, min = 20, max = 50))
```

-   $\mathbb{P}(30 \leq X \leq 40) \approx$ `r round(mean(lab_sims$x >= 30 & lab_sims$x <= 40), 3)`
-   $\mathbb{P}(X > 45) \approx$ `r round(mean(lab_sims$x > 45), 3)`
-   $\mathbb{P}(X = 35) \approx$ `r mean(lab_sims$x == 35)` (no simulated value is exactly 35)

Answers will vary slightly, but should be close to your answers in Parts b–d.
:::

### 5. A continuous mystery constant

Consider the following pdf: $$f_X(x) = \begin{cases} kx^9(1-x)^2 & \text{if } 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

#### Part a

What is the constant $k$ that makes $f_X(x)$ a valid pdf?

::: answer
$k=660$
:::

#### Part b

What is the CDF $F_X(x)$?

::: answer
Not given
:::

### 6. From a CDF to a pdf

Let $X$ be a random variable with CDF $$F_X(x)= \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } x < 0 \\ \dfrac{x^2}{4} & \text{if } 0 \leq x \leq 2 \\ 1 & \text{if } x > 2 \end{cases}$$

#### Part a

Find the pdf $f_X(x)$.

::: answer
$$f_X(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x}{2} & \text{if } 0 \leq x \leq 2 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$
:::

#### Part b

Use the CDF to find $\mathbb{P}(0.5 \leq X \leq 1.5)$.

::: answer
Not given
:::

#### Part c

Find the median of the distribution of $X$.

::: answer
Median $= \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$
:::

#### Part d

Simulate 10,000 values of $X$ with the inverse CDF method from Lesson 9, and use them to check your answers to Parts b and c.

::: answer
Not given
:::
